name: The Skarl Delving
resident: weavers and thornhounds in the galleries, silk-thieves who came for the silk and stayed, Brokk ko-Skarl who would not go home, and the Reel-Mother in the drowned shaft at the bottom
story: The Skarl cut the delving square and timbered it the clan way, following a vein of tin down into the tor for two years, until the big vein broke through into the Wold's own dark: water-worn caverns that run under the Northwold to Blackgill and further. Their spoil slid in the thaw of 1033 and buried a woodfolk boy on the path below, and the clan went home. The weavers came up through the breach into the galleries and strung them, and the biggest of them went down to the bottom, where the shaft drowned, and has been there since.
unique_object: a square clan adit, its timbering grey under years of silk, that breaks through into caverns nobody cut; and at the bottom a drowned shaft strung across with web so thick it holds a body's weight

features.note: a Skarl lamp, still hung where the shift left it

name: Under the Windthrow
resident: thornhounds and weavers in the root-galleries, poachers going through to the Wold's far side, the Warden grown in the heart-hall, and the Old Root, which is the Brother's taproot still alive and has learned to stand
story: The Brother's roots went down a thousand years into the granite's cracks and the water in them, and when the plate lifted they tore the roof off a country of their own: galleries the roots had opened, chambers where they had drunk a pool dry and gone on, the taproot's own shaft going down into the dark like a well with a tree in it. The roots did not die with the tree. The thinnest still hang from every roof, and the oldest has stood up.
unique_object: a cavern whose roof is the underside of a fallen tree's roots, hanging in curtains to the floor; and at the bottom the taproot itself, as thick as a tower, gone down into a pool and grown a face

features.note: a burner's lantern, left at the foot of the climb

name: Under Tinehold
resident: Unvowed huntsmen and knights in the hold's halls and kennels, their thornhounds, and Marshal Aubric Vane in the vigil hall at the bottom
story: Tinehold's keep stands on a cellar cut down into the scarp's granite, and the cellar on halls the order cut for itself in its first century: the knights' hall, the kennels, the long stair, the chapel where every knight's antlers were laid in a niche with his name when he died, and at the bottom the vigil hall where a knight knelt the night before he took the antlers. The Unvowed live in it as the order lived in it, more or less. They have taken the names off the niches.
unique_object: a chapel of niches cut in the granite, each with a knight's antlers laid in it and the name chiselled off; and at the bottom a vigil hall with a kneeling-stone worn into two hollows, which nobody has knelt on in twenty years
